# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 684
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/684
- **Title**: gh-683 Bug A: staging add dies on git's ignored-pathspec guard — probe-filtered pathspecs + dead dev letter fails the leg
- **Author**: IstiN
- **Branch**: `fix/683-git-add-ignored-pathspec-guard` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +416
- **Deletions**: -35
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T05:22:10Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T05:27:45Z

## PR Description

Fixes the dev-leg half of #683.

## Root cause (evidence-verified)

Failing command (run [37153405587](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/37153405587), fa gh-1206, 21:13 UTC, `factory / teammate`):

```
git add . -- ":!.dmtools/copilot-sessions" ... ":!.dmtools/credential-helper.log" ... ":!factory-kit" ":!factory-kit/**"
→ exit 1: The following paths are ignored by one of your .gitignore files:
.dmtools/credential-helper.log  .dmtools/fa-sessions  .dmtools/fa-trace.log
.dmtools/run-output.txt  .dmtools/stall-capture.log
hint: Use -f if you really want to add them.   ← advice.addIgnoredFile = git ADD's guard
```

It was **not** `git rm -r --cached --ignore-unmatch` (that command exits 0 as a silent no-op on ignored+untracked paths — verified). The killer is `git add`: its ignored-pathspec guard evaluates **`:!` exclusion pathspecs too** — naming a path that is gitignored *and exists untracked* fails the whole add. All five live droppings exist ignored-untracked in fa, and all five were named as exclusions. The timer's `git add -A -- ...` died the same way at 21:08/21:13 (`⏱️ timer: git add failed`), and the post-action's failure then exited through the success path → no PR, ticket rolled back, green run: an invisible dead dev letter (fa #1206–#1210).

Reproduced byte-for-byte locally (git 2.50): `git add . -- ":!<ignored-untracked-existing>"` → exit 1 with the exact live error; plain `git add .` → exit 0, gitignore honored. Guard does **not** fire when the ignored path is tracked (poisoned branch), nonexistent, or glob-shaped — only for a literal exclusion naming an existing ignored-untracked file.

## Fix — can never hit the guard regardless of what new runtime files appear

* `gitStaging.buildStagingPathspecs(runCommand)` (optional runner, signature-compatible): probes each artifact with `git check-ignore -q` in the same working dir —
  * ignored → exclusion **dropped** (gitignore alone keeps `git add .` away; no pathspec, no guard to trip);
  * not ignored → exclusion **kept** (the only defense there — and a not-ignored path can never trip the *ignored*-files guard).
  * probe failure → full static list (conservative, pre-fix behavior).

  All four staging sites (`developTicketAndCreatePR`, `developBugAndCreatePR`, `pushReworkChanges`, `timerAutoCommitAndSave`) pass their runner; each already runs the untrack **before** the add, so the probe observes the post-untrack state.
* `gitStaging.buildUntrackCommand()`: now `git ls-files`-scoped (`git ls-files -- <paths> | while read → git rm -r --cached --ignore-unmatch -- "$p"`) — only tracked paths are ever named to `git rm`; empty result is a true exit-0 no-op. Still one shell command (call counts unchanged).
* `developTicketAndCreatePR.js`: a Git-Operations failure (stages `Git Operations` / `Gate Fix Git Operations`) now **throws a marked error after the reset-for-retry comment** (same propagation mechanism as the fatal-CLI-environment failure) — the workflow run is RED so the SM's dead-dev-letter logic can see and retry it, instead of a green silent no-PR loop. No runner-config changes.

## Tests

`test_gitStaging` (untrack shape + probe filtering + fail-conservative), `test_developTicketAndCreatePR` (ignored-repo staging carries no runtime pathspec; Git-Operations failure throws with the marker after the reset), `test_timerAutoCommitAndSave` / `test_developBugAndCreatePR` / `test_pushReworkChanges` stubs updated for the probe + ls-files shape, plus a gh-683 ignored-repo regression test on the timer. Node harness: **1294 passed / 46 failed — failure set identical to `main`** (pre-existing node-harness gaps: `assert.doesNotThrow`, `makeDefaultConfigLoaderMock` missing in the node runner), +5 new tests.

Closes the Bug A half of #683 (fa #1206–#1210; whack-a-mole lineage gh-628 → gh-1000 → gh-683 ends here: the list stops being part of the failure surface).

Failing command (run [37153405587](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/37153405587), fa gh-1206, 21:13 UTC, `factory / teammate`):

```
git add . -- ":!.dmtools/copilot-sessions" ... ":!.dmtools/credential-helper.log" ... ":!factory-kit" ":!factory-kit/**"
→ exit 1: The following paths are ignored by one of your .gitignore files:
.dmtools/credential-helper.log  .dmtools/fa-sessions  .dmtools/fa-trace.log
.dmtools/run-output.txt  .dmtools/stall-capture.log
hint: Use -f if you really want to add them.   ← advice.addIgnoredFile = git ADD's guard
```

It was **not** `git rm -r --cached --ignore-unmatch` (that command exits 0 as a silent no-op on ignored+untracked paths — verified). The killer is `git add`: its ignored-pathspec guard evaluates **`:!` exclusion pathspecs too** — naming a path that is gitignored *and exists untracked* fails the whole add. All five live droppings exist ignored-untracked in fa, and all five were named as exclusions. The timer's `git add -A -- ...` died the same way at 21:08/21:13 (`⏱️ timer: git add failed`), and the post-action's failure then exited through the success path → no PR, ticket rolled back, green run: an invisible dead dev letter (fa #1206–#1210).

Reproduced byte-for-byte locally (git 2.50): `git add . -- ":!<ignored-untracked-existing>"` → exit 1 with the exact live error; plain `git add .` → exit 0, gitignore honored. Guard does **not** fire when the ignored path is tracked (poisoned branch), nonexistent, or glob-shaped — only for a literal exclusion naming an existing ignored-untracked file.

* `gitStaging.buildStagingPathspecs(runCommand)` (optional runner, signature-compatible): probes each artifact with `git check-ignore -q` in the same working dir —

  * not ignored → exclusion **kept** (the only defense there — and a not-ignored path can never trip the *ignored*-files guard).
  * probe failure → full static list (conservative, pre-fix behavior).

  All four staging sites (`developTicketAndCreatePR`, `developBugAndCreatePR`, `pushReworkChanges`, `timerAutoCommitAndSave`) pass their runner; each already runs the untrack **before** the add, so the probe observes the post-untrack state.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 684
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/684
- **Title**: gh-683 Bug A: staging add dies on git's ignored-pathspec guard — probe-filtered pathspecs + dead dev letter fails the leg
- **Author**: IstiN
- **Branch**: `fix/683-git-add-ignored-pathspec-guard` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +416
- **Deletions**: -35
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T05:22:10Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T05:27:45Z

## PR Description

Fixes the dev-leg half of #683.

## Root cause (evidence-verified)

Failing command (run [37153405587](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/37153405587), fa gh-1206, 21:13 UTC, `factory / teammate`):

```
git add . -- ":!.dmtools/copilot-sessions" ... ":!.dmtools/credential-helper.log" ... ":!factory-kit" ":!factory-kit/**"
→ exit 1: The following paths are ignored by one of your .gitignore files:
.dmtools/credential-helper.log  .dmtools/fa-sessions  .dmtools/fa-trace.log
.dmtools/run-output.txt  .dmtools/stall-capture.log
hint: Use -f if you really want to add them.   ← advice.addIgnoredFile = git ADD's guard
```

It was **not** `git rm -r --cached --ignore-unmatch` (that command exits 0 as a silent no-op on ignored+untracked paths — verified). The killer is `git add`: its ignored-pathspec guard evaluates **`:!` exclusion pathspecs too** — naming a path that is gitignored *and exists untracked* fails the whole add. All five live droppings exist ignored-untracked in fa, and all five were named as exclusions. The timer's `git add -A -- ...` died the same way at 21:08/21:13 (`⏱️ timer: git add failed`), and the post-action's failure then exited through the success path → no PR, ticket rolled back, green run: an invisible dead dev letter (fa #1206–#1210).

Reproduced byte-for-byte locally (git 2.50): `git add . -- ":!<ignored-untracked-existing>"` → exit 1 with the exact live error; plain `git add .` → exit 0, gitignore honored. Guard does **not** fire when the ignored path is tracked (poisoned branch), nonexistent, or glob-shaped — only for a literal exclusion naming an existing ignored-untracked file.

## Fix — can never hit the guard regardless of what new runtime files appear

* `gitStaging.buildStagingPathspecs(runCommand)` (optional runner, signature-compatible): probes each artifact with `git check-ignore -q` in the same working dir —
  * ignored → exclusion **dropped** (gitignore alone keeps `git add .` away; no pathspec, no guard to trip);
  * not ignored → exclusion **kept** (the only defense there — and a not-ignored path can never trip the *ignored*-files guard).
  * probe failure → full static list (conservative, pre-fix behavior).

  All four staging sites (`developTicketAndCreatePR`, `developBugAndCreatePR`, `pushReworkChanges`, `timerAutoCommitAndSave`) pass their runner; each already runs the untrack **before** the add, so the probe observes the post-untrack state.
* `gitStaging.buildUntrackCommand()`: now `git ls-files`-scoped (`git ls-files -- <paths> | while read → git rm -r --cached --ignore-unmatch -- "$p"`) — only tracked paths are ever named to `git rm`; empty result is a true exit-0 no-op. Still one shell command (call counts unchanged).
* `developTicketAndCreatePR.js`: a Git-Operations failure (stages `Git Operations` / `Gate Fix Git Operations`) now **throws a marked error after the reset-for-retry comment** (same propagation mechanism as the fatal-CLI-environment failure) — the workflow run is RED so the SM's dead-dev-letter logic can see and retry it, instead of a green silent no-PR loop. No runner-config changes.

## Tests

`test_gitStaging` (untrack shape + probe filtering + fail-conservative), `test_developTicketAndCreatePR` (ignored-repo staging carries no runtime pathspec; Git-Operations failure throws with the marker after the reset), `test_timerAutoCommitAndSave` / `test_developBugAndCreatePR` / `test_pushReworkChanges` stubs updated for the probe + ls-files shape, plus a gh-683 ignored-repo regression test on the timer. Node harness: **1294 passed / 46 failed — failure set identical to `main`** (pre-existing node-harness gaps: `assert.doesNotThrow`, `makeDefaultConfigLoaderMock` missing in the node runner), +5 new tests.

Closes the Bug A half of #683 (fa #1206–#1210; whack-a-mole lineage gh-628 → gh-1000 → gh-683 ends here: the list stops being part of the failure surface).

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

All four sites pass the runner. Now, let me validate the root-cause git behavior and the new untrack command shape empirically, since this is a git-behavior fix and the review should verify claims. Let me build a sandbox:

1. Create repo with .gitignore containing `.dmtools/credential-helper.log`, create the ignored-untracked file, run `git add . -- ":!.dmtools/credential-helper.log"` → expect exit 1.
2. Run `git add .` without pathspec → exit 0, file not staged.
3. Run the new untrack pipeline in a repo where a runtime path is tracked → verify it untracks; and in a clean repo → verify exit 0 no-op.
4. Test the pipeline exit code when the last tracked file's `git rm` fails — hard to force; skip. But test mid-loop failure: make `.git/hooks`? Actually simpler: not needed.
5. Test `git check-ignore -q` on a TRACKED ignored file (poisoned branch, before untrack) — the claim "tracked+ignored never trips the guard anyway" and the probe ordering. check-ignore reports 0 (ignored) even if tracked? Let me verify. If check-ignore exit 0 on a tracked file, the exclusion is dropped for a tracked+ignored file. Then `git add .` — tracked file modifications WOULD be staged (gitignore doesn't stop tracked files). But the untrack ran first, so post-untrack it's untracked → not staged. But if the untrack FAILED (caught+warned), the tracked+ignored modified log would be staged → committed → the exact gh-628 credential-leak class. That's a real (if narrow) regression scenario. Worth an IMPORTANT/SUGGESTION note: the probe drops the exclusion based on ignore-status alone, but the exclusion also protects against staging a *tracked-but-not-untracked-yet* file when the untrack step failed. Mitigation: probe should keep exclusion when `git ls-files -- <path>` reports the file as tracked (i.e., only drop when ignored AND untracked). That's a concrete, actionable improvement suggestion.

Wait, actually think again about whether dropping the exclusion for a tracked+ignored file even with successful untrack leaves any window: untrack runs BEFORE buildStagingPathspecs? Order in code: untrack command executes first (runCmd), then the add command is BUILT — the probe runs at build time, after untrack executed. Yes: `'git add . -- ' + gitStaging.buildStagingPathspecs(runCmd)` — buildStagingPathspecs is evaluated after the untrack runCmd completed. So post-untrack state observed. Good.

But there's one more subtle case: untrack succeeded for the tracked log, file becomes untracked+ignored. Probe: ignored → dropped. `git add .` — respects gitignore, skips it. The `git status --porcelain` filter isRuntimeArtifactStatusLine handles leftovers. Good.

Failure window is only when untrack fails. How could untrack fail? `git rm` on a file with local modifications staged? `git rm --cached` on a file with staged content differing from HEAD: git rm refuses "file has changes staged in the index" — wait, does --cached bypass that? Actually: `git rm --cached file` when the file has staged changes... Let me recall: git rm refuses when the file has local modifications UNLESS --cached or -f is given. With --cached it only checks... hmm, `--cached` "Use this option to unstage and remove the paths only from the index... can be combined with --ignore-unmatch". From git docs: "git rm --cached" removes from index only; it does NOT refuse due to working-tree modifications (the working tree copy is left alone). But what about staged-differs-from-HEAD? Docs: "git rm" refuses to remove files that have staged content differing from both HEAD and the working tree, and files that have been modified (unless -f). Does --cached lift that? Testing needed. The old command shape was identical though (`git rm -r --cached --ignore-unmatch <paths>`), so failure modes are the same — the PR didn't change that aspect. The difference: with the new pipeline, if a mid-loop rm fails, the pipeline exit code = that rm's code (same as old command failing). So no regression there — same behavior. The REGRESSION is only: untrack fails → probe (evaluated later) sees tracked+ignored → drops exclusion → modified tracked log gets staged. Old behavior: exclusion kept → modified tracked log NOT staged (but also not untracked — stays tracked, not committed).

Hmm wait, actually — in the OLD code with a failing untrack, the tracked+ignored MODIFIED log was excluded by pathspec from the add, so it wasn't committed. In the NEW code with a failing untrack, it gets committed (credential-helper.log onto the ticket branch — the gh-628 leak class). The probability is low (untrack failure is rare), but the blast radius is a credential-trace leak onto a public PR — the exact scenario gh-628 was about. I'd rate this IMPORTANT (not blocking — requires untrack failure first, and .gitignore'd logs leaking requires the log to be tracked AND modified AND untrack to fail).

Hmm, wait — one more scenario where probe sees tracked+ignored: what if `runCommand` probe runs in a different cwd than the add? In timer, both use workingDir. In developTicket, runCmd both. In pushRework, cmd both. In developBug, cli_execute_command both (default cwd). Consistent.

Also consider: what if check-ignore exits 0 but the path is in a directory that's ignored while individual file isn't... not relevant.

Another edge: `.dmtools/copilot-sessions` on a repo that does NOT ignore it but where the directory exists — probe exit 1 → exclusion kept → fine.

Now — the guard's "exists untracked" nuance: the probe drops the exclusion when the path is ignored EVEN IF the path doesn't exist at all. That's fine — no pathspec, no guard; gitignore keeps add away regardless.

BUT what about a repo where the path is ignored AND TRACKED (poisoned branch) and untrack SUCCEEDS (normal case)? Post-untrack: untracked+ignored → dropped exclusion → gitignore protects. Good.

What about a repo where path is ignored and tracked, untrack succeeds, but the file was ALSO the only content change... fine.

Now, the more serious question — is there any case where the probe DROPS an exclusion and the file then gets committed? Only tracked+modified+post-untrack... i.e., untrack failed (or untrack didn't cover the path — but paths come from same list). OK.

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 684
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/684
- **Title**: gh-683 Bug A: staging add dies on git's ignored-pathspec guard — probe-filtered pathspecs + dead dev letter fails the leg
- **Author**: IstiN
- **Branch**: `fix/683-git-add-ignored-pathspec-guard` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +416
- **Deletions**: -35
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T05:22:10Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T05:27:45Z

## PR Description

Fixes the dev-leg half of #683.

## Root cause (evidence-verified)

Failing command (run [37153405587](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/37153405587), fa gh-1206, 21:13 UTC, `factory / teammate`):

```
git add . -- ":!.dmtools/copilot-sessions" ... ":!.dmtools/credential-helper.log" ... ":!factory-kit" ":!factory-kit/**"
→ exit 1: The following paths are ignored by one of your .gitignore files:
.dmtools/credential-helper.log  .dmtools/fa-sessions  .dmtools/fa-trace.log
.dmtools/run-output.txt  .dmtools/stall-capture.log
hint: Use -f if you really want to add them.   ← advice.addIgnoredFile = git ADD's guard
```

It was **not** `git rm -r --cached --ignore-unmatch` (that command exits 0 as a silent no-op on ignored+untracked paths — verified). The killer is `git add`: its ignored-pathspec guard evaluates **`:!` exclusion pathspecs too** — naming a path that is gitignored *and exists untracked* fails the whole add. All five live droppings exist ignored-untracked in fa, and all five were named as exclusions. The timer's `git add -A -- ...` died the same way at 21:08/21:13 (`⏱️ timer: git add failed`), and the post-action's failure then exited through the success path → no PR, ticket rolled back, green run: an invisible dead dev letter (fa #1206–#1210).

Reproduced byte-for-byte locally (git 2.50): `git add . -- ":!<ignored-untracked-existing>"` → exit 1 with the exact live error; plain `git add .` → exit 0, gitignore honored. Guard does **not** fire when the ignored path is tracked (poisoned branch), nonexistent, or glob-shaped — only for a literal exclusion naming an existing ignored-untracked file.

## Fix — can never hit the guard regardless of what new runtime files appear

* `gitStaging.buildStagingPathspecs(runCommand)` (optional runner, signature-compatible): probes each artifact with `git check-ignore -q` in the same working dir —
  * ignored → exclusion **dropped** (gitignore alone keeps `git add .` away; no pathspec, no guard to trip);
  * not ignored → exclusion **kept** (the only defense there — and a not-ignored path can never trip the *ignored*-files guard).
  * probe failure → full static list (conservative, pre-fix behavior).

  All four staging sites (`developTicketAndCreatePR`, `developBugAndCreatePR`, `pushReworkChanges`, `timerAutoCommitAndSave`) pass their runner; each already runs the untrack **before** the add, so the probe observes the post-untrack state.
* `gitStaging.buildUntrackCommand()`: now `git ls-files`-scoped (`git ls-files -- <paths> | while read → git rm -r --cached --ignore-unmatch -- "$p"`) — only tracked paths are ever named to `git rm`; empty result is a true exit-0 no-op. Still one shell command (call counts unchanged).
* `developTicketAndCreatePR.js`: a Git-Operations failure (stages `Git Operations` / `Gate Fix Git Operations`) now **throws a marked error after the reset-for-retry comment** (same propagation mechanism as the fatal-CLI-environment failure) — the workflow run is RED so the SM's dead-dev-letter logic can see and retry it, instead of a green silent no-PR loop. No runner-config changes.

## Tests

`test_gitStaging` (untrack shape + probe filtering + fail-conservative), `test_developTicketAndCreatePR` (ignored-repo staging carries no runtime pathspec; Git-Operations failure throws with the marker after the reset), `test_timerAutoCommitAndSave` / `test_developBugAndCreatePR` / `test_pushReworkChanges` stubs updated for the probe + ls-files shape, plus a gh-683 ignored-repo regression test on the timer. Node harness: **1294 passed / 46 failed — failure set identical to `main`** (pre-existing node-harness gaps: `assert.doesNotThrow`, `makeDefaultConfigLoaderMock` missing in the node runner), +5 new tests.

Closes the Bug A half of #683 (fa #1206–#1210; whack-a-mole lineage gh-628 → gh-1000 → gh-683 ends here: the list stops being part of the failure surface).

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 684
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/684
- **Title**: gh-683 Bug A: staging add dies on git's ignored-pathspec guard — probe-filtered pathspecs + dead dev letter fails the leg
- **Author**: IstiN
- **Branch**: `fix/683-git-add-ignored-pathspec-guard` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +416
- **Deletions**: -35
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T05:22:10Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T05:27:45Z

## PR Description

Fixes the dev-leg half of #683.

## Root cause (evidence-verified)

Failing command (run [37153405587](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/37153405587), fa gh-1206, 21:13 UTC, `factory / teammate`):

```
git add . -- ":!.dmtools/copilot-sessions" ... ":!.dmtools/credential-helper.log" ... ":!factory-kit" ":!factory-kit/**"
→ exit 1: The following paths are ignored by one of your .gitignore files:
.dmtools/credential-helper.log  .dmtools/fa-sessions  .dmtools/fa-trace.log
.dmtools/run-output.txt  .dmtools/stall-capture.log
hint: Use -f if you really want to add them.   ← advice.addIgnoredFile = git ADD's guard
```

It was **not** `git rm -r --cached --ignore-unmatch` (that command exits 0 as a silent no-op on ignored+untracked paths — verified). The killer is `git add`: its ignored-pathspec guard evaluates **`:!` exclusion pathspecs too** — naming a path that is gitignored *and exists untracked* fails the whole add. All five live droppings exist ignored-untracked in fa, and all five were named as exclusions. The timer's `git add -A -- ...` died the same way at 21:08/21:13 (`⏱️ timer: git add failed`), and the post-action's failure then exited through the success path → no PR, ticket rolled back, green run: an invisible dead dev letter (fa #1206–#1210).

Reproduced byte-for-byte locally (git 2.50): `git add . -- ":!<ignored-untracked-existing>"` → exit 1 with the exact live error; plain `git add .` → exit 0, gitignore honored. Guard does **not** fire when the ignored path is tracked (poisoned branch), nonexistent, or glob-shaped — only for a literal exclusion naming an existing ignored-untracked file.

## Fix — can never hit the guard regardless of what new runtime files appear

* `gitStaging.buildStagingPathspecs(runCommand)` (optional runner, signature-compatible): probes each artifact with `git check-ignore -q` in the same working dir —
  * ignored → exclusion **dropped** (gitignore alone keeps `git add .` away; no pathspec, no guard to trip);
  * not ignored → exclusion **kept** (the only defense there — and a not-ignored path can never trip the *ignored*-files guard).
  * probe failure → full static list (conservative, pre-fix behavior).

  All four staging sites (`developTicketAndCreatePR`, `developBugAndCreatePR`, `pushReworkChanges`, `timerAutoCommitAndSave`) pass their runner; each already runs the untrack **before** the add, so the probe observes the post-untrack state.
* `gitStaging.buildUntrackCommand()`: now `git ls-files`-scoped (`git ls-files -- <paths> | while read → git rm -r --cached --ignore-unmatch -- "$p"`) — only tracked paths are ever named to `git rm`; empty result is a true exit-0 no-op. Still one shell command (call counts unchanged).
* `developTicketAndCreatePR.js`: a Git-Operations failure (stages `Git Operations` / `Gate Fix Git Operations`) now **throws a marked error after the reset-for-retry comment** (same propagation mechanism as the fatal-CLI-environment failure) — the workflow run is RED so the SM's dead-dev-letter logic can see and retry it, instead of a green silent no-PR loop. No runner-config changes.

## Tests

`test_gitStaging` (untrack shape + probe filtering + fail-conservative), `test_developTicketAndCreatePR` (ignored-repo staging carries no runtime pathspec; Git-Operations failure throws with the marker after the reset), `test_timerAutoCommitAndSave` / `test_developBugAndCreatePR` / `test_pushReworkChanges` stubs updated for the probe + ls-files shape, plus a gh-683 ignored-repo regression test on the timer. Node harness: **1294 passed / 46 failed — failure set identical to `main`** (pre-existing node-harness gaps: `assert.doesNotThrow`, `makeDefaultConfigLoaderMock` missing in the node runner), +5 new tests.

Closes the Bug A half of #683 (fa #1206–#1210; whack-a-mole lineage gh-628 → gh-1000 → gh-683 ends here: the list stops being part of the failure surface).

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

Very interesting! `git check-ignore -q -- <tracked+ignored file>` exits **1** (not ignored) — check-ignore only reports paths that are NOT tracked... wait, actually the documented behavior: "check-ignore ... For each pathname given via the command-line or from a file via --stdin, check whether the file is excluded by .gitignore". Note from git docs: tracked files are not reported as ignored (actually, the git docs say: "Note that this does not check whether the file is tracked; by default it only checks the ignore rules"... hmm but the empirical result here shows exit 1 for a TRACKED file matching the ignore pattern).

Actually, git 2.30+ behavior: `git check-ignore` shows the path as ignored ONLY if it would be excluded — and for TRACKED files, gitignore does not apply (tracked files are never ignored), so check-ignore reports not-ignored. Let me confirm: yes, empirically exit=1 on tracked+ignored. That's good news for the fix:

- On a poisoned branch (tracked+ignored log), the probe returns "not ignored" → exclusion KEPT → `git add .` does not stage the tracked modified log (exclusion blocks it). Then the untrack... wait, order: untrack FIRST, then probe. Post-untrack it's untracked → probe exit 0 → exclusion dropped → gitignore protects. The sequencing works and my earlier concern shrinks further:

Failure window re-analysis: untrack FAILS (rare) + file tracked+modified → probe sees tracked+ignored → check-ignore exit 1 → exclusion KEPT → modified log NOT staged. The regression scenario I hypothesized earlier doesn't exist because check-ignore reports tracked files as NOT ignored! The probe naturally keeps the exclusion for tracked files.

Wait — but is that right? Let me double check the earlier sequence. In step 3, I did `git add -f` + commit, then check-ignore exit 1. Yes — tracked → not reported as ignored. (This matches git's documented behavior since 2.x: check-ignore checks against the index too? Actually what it does: "the pathname is checked... Note that tracked files are not checked against ignore rules" — empirically confirmed.)

So the probe+order design is actually sound:
- tracked+ignored → probe exit 1 → exclusion kept → tracked modifications never staged by the broad add; untrack (running before) removes from index → afterwards untracked+ignored.
- If untrack failed but file is still tracked → probe exit 1 → exclusion kept → safe (no leak).
- untracked+ignored → probe exit 0 → dropped → gitignore protects, guard can't fire.
- not ignored → kept → exclusion is the only defense; guard can't fire on a non-ignored path.
- probe infrastructure failure (exit 128) → exception → kept (conservative).

The design is solid. My earlier hypothesized regression is invalid. Good — verified by experiment.

Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 684
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/684
- **Title**: gh-683 Bug A: staging add dies on git's ignored-pathspec guard — probe-filtered pathspecs + dead dev letter fails the leg
- **Author**: IstiN
- **Branch**: `fix/683-git-add-ignored-pathspec-guard` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +416
- **Deletions**: -35
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T05:22:10Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T05:27:45Z

## PR Description

Fixes the dev-leg half of #683.

## Root cause (evidence-verified)

Failing command (run [37153405587](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/37153405587), fa gh-1206, 21:13 UTC, `factory / teammate`):

```
git add . -- ":!.dmtools/copilot-sessions" ... ":!.dmtools/credential-helper.log" ... ":!factory-kit" ":!factory-kit/**"
→ exit 1: The following paths are ignored by one of your .gitignore files:
.dmtools/credential-helper.log  .dmtools/fa-sessions  .dmtools/fa-trace.log
.dmtools/run-output.txt  .dmtools/stall-capture.log
hint: Use -f if you really want to add them.   ← advice.addIgnoredFile = git ADD's guard
```

It was **not** `git rm -r --cached --ignore-unmatch` (that command exits 0 as a silent no-op on ignored+untracked paths — verified). The killer is `git add`: its ignored-pathspec guard evaluates **`:!` exclusion pathspecs too** — naming a path that is gitignored *and exists untracked* fails the whole add. All five live droppings exist ignored-untracked in fa, and all five were named as exclusions. The timer's `git add -A -- ...` died the same way at 21:08/21:13 (`⏱️ timer: git add failed`), and the post-action's failure then exited through the success path → no PR, ticket rolled back, green run: an invisible dead dev letter (fa #1206–#1210).

Reproduced byte-for-byte locally (git 2.50): `git add . -- ":!<ignored-untracked-existing>"` → exit 1 with the exact live error; plain `git add .` → exit 0, gitignore honored. Guard does **not** fire when the ignored path is tracked (poisoned branch), nonexistent, or glob-shaped — only for a literal exclusion naming an existing ignored-untracked file.

## Fix — can never hit the guard regardless of what new runtime files appear

* `gitStaging.buildStagingPathspecs(runCommand)` (optional runner, signature-compatible): probes each artifact with `git check-ignore -q` in the same working dir —
  * ignored → exclusion **dropped** (gitignore alone keeps `git add .` away; no pathspec, no guard to trip);
  * not ignored → exclusion **kept** (the only defense there — and a not-ignored path can never trip the *ignored*-files guard).
  * probe failure → full static list (conservative, pre-fix behavior).

  All four staging sites (`developTicketAndCreatePR`, `developBugAndCreatePR`, `pushReworkChanges`, `timerAutoCommitAndSave`) pass their runner; each already runs the untrack **before** the add, so the probe observes the post-untrack state.
* `gitStaging.buildUntrackCommand()`: now `git ls-files`-scoped (`git ls-files -- <paths> | while read → git rm -r --cached --ignore-unmatch -- "$p"`) — only tracked paths are ever named to `git rm`; empty result is a true exit-0 no-op. Still one shell command (call counts unchanged).
* `developTicketAndCreatePR.js`: a Git-Operations failure (stages `Git Operations` / `Gate Fix Git Operations`) now **throws a marked error after the reset-for-retry comment** (same propagation mechanism as the fatal-CLI-environment failure) — the workflow run is RED so the SM's dead-dev-letter logic can see and retry it, instead of a green silent no-PR loop. No runner-config changes.

## Tests

`test_gitStaging` (untrack shape + probe filtering + fail-conservative), `test_developTicketAndCreatePR` (ignored-repo staging carries no runtime pathspec; Git-Operations failure throws with the marker after the reset), `test_timerAutoCommitAndSave` / `test_developBugAndCreatePR` / `test_pushReworkChanges` stubs updated for the probe + ls-files shape, plus a gh-683 ignored-repo regression test on the timer. Node harness: **1294 passed / 46 failed — failure set identical to `main`** (pre-existing node-harness gaps: `assert.doesNotThrow`, `makeDefaultConfigLoaderMock` missing in the node runner), +5 new tests.

Closes the Bug A half of #683 (fa #1206–#1210; whack-a-mole lineage gh-628 → gh-1000 → gh-683 ends here: the list stops being part of the failure surface).
